families.name: Source revisions and edit conflicts
families.scope: Allowlisted source reads, controlled editor drafts and confirmed local source saves.
families.refusal: For the selected source operation, reject unsupported targets or stale revision preconditions before changing source or creating backups.
families.recovery: Preserve pre-operation source bytes and affected drafts on refusal; require an explicit action before replacing a retained draft.
families.feedback: Expose current source revision in read or conflict responses and loaded revision in the controlled editor when applicable.
families.evidence: Exercise matching and stale revisions, comparing declared responses, source bytes, retained drafts and backup effects for the selected operation.

capabilities.title: Read source content revisions
capabilities.outcome: Every successful allowlisted source read returns a SHA-256 revision computed from exact on-disk source bytes without normalization or source modification.

capabilities.title: Retain editor base revisions
capabilities.outcome: Loading a controlled source editor binds its draft to the returned revision, and typing changes the draft without changing that baseline.

capabilities.title: Refuse stale confirmed source writes
capabilities.outcome: A confirmed save with a stale baseRevision returns a conflict before creating backups, promoting content or changing the current source file.

capabilities.title: Preserve drafts after source conflicts
capabilities.outcome: A rejected stale save leaves the complete unsaved editor draft intact and displays an explicit source conflict requiring an operator decision.

capabilities.title: Reload current source explicitly
capabilities.outcome: After a conflict, an explicit reload fetches the latest file and revision, replacing the draft only through that disclosed operator action.

capabilities.title: Compare draft and current source
capabilities.outcome: A conflict comparison shows the retained draft beside current source with their respective revisions, identifying changed lines without automatically choosing either version.

capabilities.title: Detect externally removed source
capabilities.outcome: When an opened file is removed externally, the editor reports its unavailable state and retains the draft without recreating the file.

capabilities.title: Detect source identity replacement
capabilities.outcome: Replacing an opened file at the same path invalidates its previous baseline whenever content differs, preventing an unnoticed overwrite of the replacement.

capabilities.title: Confirm intentional conflict replacement
capabilities.outcome: An operator can preview an intentional overwrite against the latest revision, then separately confirm only that current replacement while preserving backup evidence.

capabilities.title: Track source revision after text saves
capabilities.outcome: A successful guarded leaf-text save refreshes the mapped file revision and prevents another open editor from silently saving its older source baseline.

capabilities.title: Refresh revisions after guarded font changes
capabilities.outcome: Saving a confirmed project font change exposes the new stylesheet revision so open stylesheet drafts can detect the resulting external source change.

capabilities.title: Bind previews to source baselines
capabilities.outcome: A source draft preview records its baseline revision and reports when the real source advances, without promoting preview content into the repository.

capabilities.title: Report no-op source saves
capabilities.outcome: Saving content identical to current source returns a clear no-change result and preserves the current revision without creating redundant backups.

capabilities.title: Distinguish revision and transport failures
capabilities.outcome: The editor presents revision conflicts separately from unavailable network or server responses, preserving drafts and exposing a suitable next action for each.

capabilities.title: Expire revision baselines on target switches
capabilities.outcome: Switching files binds the new draft to its own revision and cannot reuse a previous file revision to authorize the newly selected target.

capabilities.title: Recover revision-bound local drafts
capabilities.outcome: An opted-in local draft recovery record retains its source path and baseline revision, and reopening compares that baseline before offering restoration.

capabilities.title: Export a conflict comparison
capabilities.outcome: An operator can download a bounded comparison containing path, revisions and explicit draft content after seeing the export scope and confirming inclusion.

capabilities.title: Inspect source revision history
capabilities.outcome: A local history view lists revisions associated with confirmed source operations and distinguishes observed external changes from builder-authored saves.

capabilities.title: Reject malformed source revisions
capabilities.outcome: Save requests containing malformed or wrong-length revision values receive a structured validation error before reading unrelated paths or creating any backup.

capabilities.title: Explain revision scope to operators
capabilities.outcome: Source help explains that content hashes detect changed bytes for one allowed file and do not establish Git cleanliness, provider publication or exclusive ownership.

families.name: Source access and path policy
families.scope: Repository-relative source selection, read eligibility and guarded write-path decisions.
families.refusal: Refuse linked paths, traversal, unsupported extensions and private/runtime targets with contained errors.
families.recovery: Keep the previous valid selection when a requested path is refused or disappears.
families.feedback: Explain read eligibility and supported write kinds without exposing private directory inventories.
families.evidence: Use temporary repositories with symlinks, path aliases, case differences and allowlist boundaries.

capabilities.title: Browse eligible source files
capabilities.outcome: A source browser lists only regular repository files allowed by the current policy, with bounded results and explicit omissions for oversized inventories.

capabilities.title: Filter source by allowed extension
capabilities.outcome: Operators can filter the eligible source list by supported extension without making excluded file types readable or changing the underlying access policy.

capabilities.title: Explain source path refusals
capabilities.outcome: A refused path produces a stable reason category describing the policy boundary while avoiding disclosure of neighboring private filenames or file content.

capabilities.title: Resolve repository-relative source paths
capabilities.outcome: The source picker accepts canonical repository-relative paths and visibly rejects absolute paths, traversal segments or ambiguous encodings before issuing a file operation.

capabilities.title: Detect linked source ancestors
capabilities.outcome: Source inspection refuses files reached through linked parent directories even when the final filename appears allowlisted and remains inside the displayed path.

capabilities.title: Identify supported source write kinds
capabilities.outcome: Each eligible file reports whether literal text, font imports or other reviewed write kinds are supported, with unsupported structural edits clearly unavailable.

capabilities.title: Display source size before opening
capabilities.outcome: The picker displays bounded file-size metadata and refuses an oversized read with its applicable limit instead of partially presenting content as complete.

capabilities.title: Separate generated and authored files
capabilities.outcome: Eligible generated files carry a generated-origin label and remain read-only unless a reviewed ownership rule explicitly designates the corresponding writable artifact.

capabilities.title: Protect runtime and backup paths
capabilities.outcome: Runtime state, temporary ingest, operation logs and source backups remain absent from normal source browsing and cannot be reached by manipulating picker queries.

capabilities.title: Handle source case differences
capabilities.outcome: Source lookup preserves exact tracked path casing and reports ambiguous case aliases without selecting a different file on case-insensitive platforms.

capabilities.title: Retain safe selections across refresh
capabilities.outcome: Refreshing the eligible inventory preserves a still-valid selected file and clears an invalid selection without activating another row at the previous position.

capabilities.title: Search source metadata
capabilities.outcome: Operators can search eligible filenames and declared source tags without indexing file bodies, environment contents, secrets or temporary execution records.

capabilities.title: Inspect source rule provenance
capabilities.outcome: A source policy view names the active allowlist rule for an eligible file and distinguishes that rule from a future proposed access expansion.

capabilities.title: Preview a path policy proposal
capabilities.outcome: An operator can inspect the exact paths affected by a proposed allowlist change in a temporary review without applying that change or opening files.

capabilities.title: Compare source access policies
capabilities.outcome: A read-only comparison shows added and removed path rules between two reviewed policy revisions, including which existing selections would lose eligibility.

capabilities.title: Handle unavailable source encodings
capabilities.outcome: Source reads report unsupported encodings explicitly and preserve existing drafts, rather than replacing invalid bytes or presenting a lossy decoding as authoritative content.

capabilities.title: Bound source directory traversal
capabilities.outcome: Eligible-file enumeration has declared depth and file-count budgets, reports truncation and avoids following recursive links or expanding excluded directory trees.

capabilities.title: Show source access by workspace
capabilities.outcome: The source picker displays its selected repository boundary and never combines eligible inventories from different workspaces into a single writable selection.

capabilities.title: Remember nonsecret source navigation
capabilities.outcome: Optional picker preferences retain only eligible path and filter metadata; reopening revalidates those paths before reading content or enabling any operation.

capabilities.title: Export an eligible source inventory
capabilities.outcome: An explicit inventory export contains only public eligible path metadata and policy decisions, excluding file bodies, private paths, runtime values and credentials.

families.name: Durable document and node identity
families.scope: Stable identities for imported pages, nodes and references across reviewed reimports.
families.refusal: Reject duplicate identities, invalid references and ambiguous identity matches without choosing a target silently.
families.recovery: Preserve the prior accepted identity map when reconciliation fails and expose unresolved candidates.
families.feedback: Distinguish durable source identity from transient DOM references and display reconciliation decisions.
families.evidence: Reimport reordered and replaced fixtures and verify stable references, ambiguity refusal and no source mutation.

capabilities.title: Assign stable document identities
capabilities.outcome: Importing the same declared document twice produces the same durable identity while separate declared source documents receive distinct identities within the selected workspace.

capabilities.title: Assign stable page identities
capabilities.outcome: Pages retain durable identifiers across label changes and inventory order changes when their reviewed source identity remains unchanged in the same workspace.

capabilities.title: Assign stable node identities
capabilities.outcome: Imported nodes receive durable identifiers tied to reviewed source anchors, and a repeated import preserves those identifiers without depending on live DOM object references.

capabilities.title: Reject duplicate node identifiers
capabilities.outcome: Import validation reports every duplicate node identifier within its bounded document scope and leaves the previously accepted graph and source files unchanged.

capabilities.title: Preserve identity across sibling reorder
capabilities.outcome: Reordering compatible source siblings preserves their durable identifiers and updates order references without confusing two elements that share the same visible label.

capabilities.title: Reconcile renamed source files
capabilities.outcome: A proposed source-file rename displays identity match evidence and ambiguity before an operator accepts transferring existing document references to the new source path.

capabilities.title: Distinguish replacement from modification
capabilities.outcome: Reimport distinguishes a replaced source object from a modification when its identity evidence changes, preventing old comments or commands from silently targeting the replacement.

capabilities.title: Resolve explicit authored identifiers
capabilities.outcome: A supported authored identity annotation becomes an import anchor only after validation of uniqueness, permitted syntax and its relationship to the selected source document.

capabilities.title: Bound fallback identity matching
capabilities.outcome: Imports report when stable annotations are absent and use a documented bounded matching rule, leaving ambiguous matches unresolved instead of assigning arbitrary previous identities.

capabilities.title: Inspect identity provenance
capabilities.outcome: Selecting a durable object reveals which source anchor or document allocation established its identity and whether the current live preview has a matching representation.

capabilities.title: Maintain identity aliases during migration
capabilities.outcome: A reviewed migration can record a retired identifier alias with its replacement and provenance, while rejecting loops or aliases that resolve outside the selected document.

capabilities.title: Reject cross-document identity confusion
capabilities.outcome: A command addressed to one document cannot resolve a matching node identifier in another document, even when both source trees contain identical labels or routes.

capabilities.title: Invalidate identities after workspace switches
capabilities.outcome: Switching workspaces discards transient lookup caches and revalidates durable references against the new workspace identity rather than reusing previous source path matches.

capabilities.title: Locate objects by durable reference
capabilities.outcome: A bounded lookup resolves a qualified durable document and node reference to its current read model or returns an explicit missing or ambiguous result.

capabilities.title: Report orphaned durable references
capabilities.outcome: Reimport lists references whose target no longer exists and preserves their original provenance, without attaching those records to a nearby node automatically.

capabilities.title: Compare identity maps before import
capabilities.outcome: A reconciliation preview lists preserved, added, retired and ambiguous identifiers before accepting an import, with stable counts and downloadable bounded metadata.

capabilities.title: Version identity mapping rules
capabilities.outcome: Identity mappings declare the reconciliation rule version that produced them so a later importer can propose an explicit migration rather than silently reinterpret anchors.

capabilities.title: Preserve identities in document export
capabilities.outcome: Exporting and reopening a compatible document retains durable identifiers and qualified references while clearing transient DOM handles and session-specific runtime metadata.

capabilities.title: Test identity collision isolation
capabilities.outcome: Two temporary repositories with matching relative source paths receive workspace-qualified identities that cannot authorize commands against each other's imported objects or source files.

capabilities.title: Explain identity confidence
capabilities.outcome: The object inspector distinguishes explicit authored identity, reviewed migration and heuristic matching confidence so an operator understands why an object is writable or unresolved.

families.name: Source ownership and mapping
families.scope: Object ownership modes, supported source spans and write responsibility.
families.refusal: Refuse edits with ambiguous spans, mixed ownership or unsupported adapters before proposing source changes.
families.recovery: Preserve source authority and previously accepted mappings when a new mapping cannot be validated.
families.feedback: Label source-owned, document-owned, hybrid-controlled and unmapped objects with supported operations.
families.evidence: Compare mapping fixtures against exact source spans and verify unrelated content remains unchanged.

capabilities.title: Label source-owned objects
capabilities.outcome: Imported objects identify their source-owned mode and explain that authored repository content remains authoritative, with only declared supported semantic operations available for editing.

capabilities.title: Label document-owned artifacts
capabilities.outcome: Generated artifacts identify their owning document and output boundary so an operator can distinguish supported regeneration from direct edits to unrelated authored files.

capabilities.title: Label hybrid ownership boundaries
capabilities.outcome: A hybrid-controlled object declares which fields belong to source and which belong to its document, and unsupported overlapping edits remain unavailable until reviewed.

capabilities.title: Expose unmapped preview elements
capabilities.outcome: Selecting an unmapped preview element shows its runtime location and unavailable source-write state instead of inventing a source path from its visible text.

capabilities.title: Inspect exact source spans
capabilities.outcome: A mapped object can reveal the bounded source span and its content revision that support its current editable fields, without opening unrelated files.

capabilities.title: Show adapter write capabilities
capabilities.outcome: The ownership inspector lists the installed adapter's supported literal, style, structure or generated operations and marks all other operation kinds as unsupported for the selection.

capabilities.title: Refuse ambiguous literal mappings
capabilities.outcome: A literal-text edit with multiple compatible source occurrences displays the ambiguity and retains the draft rather than choosing the first matching occurrence in the file.

capabilities.title: Detect mapping revision drift
capabilities.outcome: A source mapping becomes stale when its bound file revision changes, and the inspector requires reconciliation before enabling another mapped source write for that object.

capabilities.title: Map shared shell elements
capabilities.outcome: Supported header, footer and navigation selections resolve to their declared shared source owner, making the broader impact visible before a guarded shared-file change.

capabilities.title: Map route-specific content
capabilities.outcome: Supported page selections resolve through the current route and reviewed page inventory, keeping identical text on different pages associated with its own source owner.

capabilities.title: Inspect generated output provenance
capabilities.outcome: Selecting an eligible generated artifact shows the source document, generator version and output revision that produced it, without treating that provenance as permission to regenerate.

capabilities.title: Preview ownership changes
capabilities.outcome: An ownership migration proposal lists objects, fields and source paths whose authority would change and requires separate acceptance before altering any active mapping.

capabilities.title: Detect conflicting owner claims
capabilities.outcome: Two adapters claiming write authority over the same source span produce an explicit conflict that disables writes while leaving both claims visible for review.

capabilities.title: Separate instance and definition ownership
capabilities.outcome: A component instance inspector distinguishes instance-owned properties from definition-owned structure so editing an instance cannot silently modify every use of its shared definition.

capabilities.title: Track read-only source regions
capabilities.outcome: Unsupported expressions and opaque source regions retain their exact source ownership metadata and remain inspectable without being converted into editable generated content during import.

capabilities.title: Respect external component ownership
capabilities.outcome: An externally authored component retains its external source owner and supported property contract, while its internal structure stays read-only in the visual designer.

capabilities.title: Compare mapping coverage
capabilities.outcome: A bounded report counts mapped, partially mapped, stale and unmapped objects in the selected document, exposing excluded scope instead of claiming complete source coverage.

capabilities.title: Explain operation impact ownership
capabilities.outcome: Before a supported operation, the inspector identifies every declared source owner and shared artifact affected, with unavailable ownership evidence blocking the proposed write.

capabilities.title: Validate source maps after promotion
capabilities.outcome: After a confirmed source change, the adapter revalidates affected mappings against the promoted revision and reports unresolved spans without repairing unrelated source automatically.

capabilities.title: Export ownership diagnostics
capabilities.outcome: An explicit diagnostics export contains qualified object identifiers, ownership modes and bounded source metadata while excluding source bodies, credentials, private runtime paths and session tokens.

families.name: Canonical document graph
families.scope: Normalized document read models, graph invariants and bounded import structure.
families.refusal: Reject cycles, broken references, unsupported schema versions and oversized graphs without partial acceptance.
families.recovery: Retain the previous accepted document and return complete bounded diagnostics when an import fails.
families.feedback: Display graph version, revision, object counts and unsupported imported regions distinctly.
families.evidence: Validate literal graph fixtures including cycles, reparenting, schema migration and repeated import.

capabilities.title: Import a normalized document read model
capabilities.outcome: A supported import produces a normalized document containing explicit page, node and reference collections while preserving source-owned objects and performing no source write.

capabilities.title: Validate document root references
capabilities.outcome: Every imported page resolves to an existing root node in the same document, and a missing or cross-document root prevents accepting the new graph.

capabilities.title: Reject cyclic node hierarchies
capabilities.outcome: Graph validation detects a node ancestry cycle and reports its bounded reference path without hanging traversal or modifying the previously accepted document state.

capabilities.title: Validate parent child reciprocity
capabilities.outcome: Each parent-child relationship agrees in both directions, and mismatches are reported as import errors rather than silently repaired by assigning a different parent.

capabilities.title: Preserve child ordering
capabilities.outcome: The canonical graph stores explicit sibling order, and exporting then reopening a valid document reproduces the same order without depending on object-key enumeration.

capabilities.title: Represent opaque imported nodes
capabilities.outcome: Unsupported source regions appear as labeled opaque nodes with preserved source references, preventing the designer from claiming editable structure it cannot safely round-trip.

capabilities.title: Bound document import size
capabilities.outcome: Imports enforce declared byte, node, reference and depth budgets and report the exceeded limit before accepting a partial or silently truncated canonical document.

capabilities.title: Validate document schema versions
capabilities.outcome: A document declares its schema version, and unsupported future versions receive an actionable refusal without being downgraded or rewritten using the current schema.

capabilities.title: Compute canonical document revisions
capabilities.outcome: Equivalent normalized documents produce the same canonical revision regardless of insignificant JSON key order, while meaningful field or sibling-order changes alter the revision.

capabilities.title: Inspect graph validation findings
capabilities.outcome: Operators can filter bounded validation findings by severity, object and reference type, with stable identifiers linking each finding to the affected imported object.

capabilities.title: Separate runtime from canonical fields
capabilities.outcome: Live DOM handles, process identifiers, session tokens and temporary preview coordinates never become serialized canonical document fields or affect its durable content revision.

capabilities.title: Resolve qualified document references
capabilities.outcome: Graph lookups require a document-qualified reference and return exactly one compatible object, with missing or wrong-kind targets producing explicit typed errors.

capabilities.title: Retain unsupported schema extensions
capabilities.outcome: A reviewed extension namespace can preserve unknown read-only metadata without turning those fields into executable commands or silently claiming the current editor understands them.

capabilities.title: Compare canonical graph revisions
capabilities.outcome: A read-only comparison reports added, removed, changed and reordered objects between two accepted graph revisions while preserving both original normalized documents unchanged.

capabilities.title: Migrate documents through reviewed steps
capabilities.outcome: A schema migration preview lists its ordered transformations and unsupported fields, then applies only the explicitly accepted version transition in an isolated working copy.

capabilities.title: Validate component references
capabilities.outcome: Every declared component reference resolves to a compatible definition version or remains an explicit unresolved dependency that blocks operations requiring that component's structure.

capabilities.title: Validate collection references
capabilities.outcome: Collection references declare an expected schema identity and version, and incompatible or missing schemas prevent accepting bindings that depend on their fields or relationships.

capabilities.title: Serialize documents deterministically
capabilities.outcome: Repeated serialization of an unchanged canonical graph produces identical bytes with documented ordering, without adding timestamps or host-specific paths to the reusable document representation.

capabilities.title: Inspect document graph statistics
capabilities.outcome: A bounded graph summary reports page, node, component, collection and unresolved-reference counts using the accepted graph revision as the explicit calculation basis.

capabilities.title: Recover the previous valid graph
capabilities.outcome: A failed reimport leaves the previous accepted graph available for inspection and explains which new source revision could not be reconciled into a valid document.

families.name: Versioned API contracts
families.scope: Typed LAN query and command envelopes with explicit capability versions.
families.refusal: Reject unsupported versions, unknown fields and invalid payloads before domain code can mutate state.
families.recovery: Return structured failures with request identity and preserve previous valid client state.
families.feedback: Expose schema versions, supported operations and actionable field-level validation messages.
families.evidence: Exercise contract fixtures, unsupported versions, malformed input and compatibility negotiation without provider access.

capabilities.title: Advertise the LAN API version
capabilities.outcome: A local discovery response declares the current API contract version and compatible client versions, without implying every planned command is implemented or currently authorized.

capabilities.title: Expose query contract descriptors
capabilities.outcome: Each implemented query advertises its input schema, bounded result shape and read scope so clients can discover supported inspection operations without executing arbitrary server functions.

capabilities.title: Expose command contract descriptors
capabilities.outcome: Each implemented command declares required capability, confirmation, revision preconditions and effect scope, while unimplemented command descriptors remain explicitly unavailable for execution.

capabilities.title: Validate exact command envelopes
capabilities.outcome: A command request accepts only its declared envelope fields and reports unknown or incorrectly typed fields before resolving a target or changing local state.

capabilities.title: Validate query input schemas
capabilities.outcome: Invalid query parameters receive bounded structured field errors instead of being coerced into different filters, paths, identifiers or result limits without operator visibility.

capabilities.title: Negotiate compatible client contracts
capabilities.outcome: A client with a supported older contract can discover compatible operations and unavailable newer fields without silently invoking a different version of an existing command.

capabilities.title: Refuse unsupported API versions
capabilities.outcome: Requests for an unsupported API version return a stable incompatibility result that identifies supported versions and leaves the selected repository and current client state unchanged.

capabilities.title: Publish typed error categories
capabilities.outcome: Contract responses distinguish validation, missing target, conflict, capability, confirmation and internal failures with stable machine-readable categories and bounded operator-facing explanations for each case.

capabilities.title: Validate response contracts
capabilities.outcome: Development checks detect a server response that violates its declared result schema and report the endpoint and mismatch without substituting fabricated successful data in the client.

capabilities.title: Define pagination contracts
capabilities.outcome: Paginated queries declare cursor or offset behavior, maximum page size and total-count scope, with malformed pagination rejected rather than silently reinterpreted as another page.

capabilities.title: Version capability identifiers
capabilities.outcome: Capability descriptors use stable versioned identities, allowing a client to detect a changed operation contract without relying on a translated button label or route filename.

capabilities.title: Separate read and mutation contracts
capabilities.outcome: Query envelopes cannot request mutations through hidden flags, and command envelopes always expose their effect and required authority before being accepted by domain handlers.

capabilities.title: Describe contract deprecations
capabilities.outcome: Discovery metadata identifies deprecated contracts, supported replacement operations and the expected compatibility window while existing supported behavior remains documented until an explicit removal release.

capabilities.title: Inspect contract examples locally
capabilities.outcome: Operators can view synthetic valid and invalid request examples for a selected contract without sending those examples or storing project-specific values in reusable contract files.

capabilities.title: Validate union payload discriminators
capabilities.outcome: Requests containing a mismatched command kind and payload variant fail validation before their fields are passed to a handler for a different supported operation.

capabilities.title: Bound validation diagnostics
capabilities.outcome: Schema validation returns a declared maximum number of findings with an omitted-count indicator, preventing maliciously large payloads from producing unbounded error responses or logs.

capabilities.title: Define nullable and absent semantics
capabilities.outcome: Contract documentation and validators distinguish an absent field from an explicit null value, and each accepted form produces the documented effect without accidental defaulting.

capabilities.title: Inspect contract compatibility changes
capabilities.outcome: A local comparison lists breaking and additive schema changes between reviewed API versions so an operator can assess affected clients before selecting a new contract set.

capabilities.title: Export public contract metadata
capabilities.outcome: An explicit contract export contains only reviewed public schemas and capability descriptors, excluding session authority, machine paths, provider configuration and private runtime values from the archive.

capabilities.title: Bind tests to contract versions
capabilities.outcome: A contract test receipt names the exact API schema revision and implemented operation set it exercised, keeping generated type availability separate from accepted runtime behavior.

families.name: Transport and request lifecycle
families.scope: Loopback HTTP handling, request bounds, cancellation and correlated responses.
families.refusal: Reject invalid hosts, origins, content types, methods and oversized bodies before dispatch.
families.recovery: Cancel or time out only owned request work and retain client drafts after interrupted communication.
families.feedback: Show request progress, cancellation, retry eligibility and sanitized correlation identifiers.
families.evidence: Use temporary local servers for split bodies, disconnects, invalid headers, timeouts and duplicate submissions.

capabilities.title: Assign request correlation identifiers
capabilities.outcome: Every accepted local request receives a bounded nonsecret correlation identifier that connects its response and sanitized diagnostics without disclosing session tokens or source content.

capabilities.title: Enforce declared HTTP methods
capabilities.outcome: Each endpoint accepts only its declared methods and returns an explicit method refusal for unsupported verbs without invoking a domain handler or changing any local state.

capabilities.title: Validate JSON content types
capabilities.outcome: Mutation endpoints require their documented JSON content type and reject incompatible bodies before parsing them as commands or accepting content from unintended browser submission formats.

capabilities.title: Bound request body bytes
capabilities.outcome: The local transport counts incoming body bytes against a declared limit and terminates oversized input with a structured refusal before domain validation or backup creation.

capabilities.title: Handle incomplete request bodies
capabilities.outcome: A client disconnecting midway through a body produces a canceled request outcome and cannot leave partial domain state, temporary source output or a successful operation receipt.

capabilities.title: Enforce request parse deadlines
capabilities.outcome: A request exceeding its documented body-read deadline is canceled and reported without blocking subsequent local inspection requests or treating incomplete payload bytes as a valid command.

capabilities.title: Reject invalid host headers
capabilities.outcome: Requests with host values outside the active loopback authority receive a refusal before serving dashboard content, contract data, source files or mutation endpoints for another authority.

capabilities.title: Reject mismatched browser origins
capabilities.outcome: Origin-bearing requests outside the active LAN and selected Vite origins fail closed while preserving the current local session and its existing authorized request behavior.

capabilities.title: Distinguish transport and domain errors
capabilities.outcome: Clients receive separate transport-failure and domain-refusal states so they can retain drafts and avoid presenting an unavailable server as a rejected source revision or invalid document.

capabilities.title: Cancel obsolete read requests
capabilities.outcome: Switching a selected file or document cancels the client's obsolete read request and prevents its later response from replacing the new selection's state or revision baseline.

capabilities.title: Ignore stale response generations
capabilities.outcome: Responses carry enough request context for the client to discard an older generation after a newer accepted read, preserving the latest selected target and unsaved draft.

capabilities.title: Advertise safe retry semantics
capabilities.outcome: An operation descriptor indicates whether retry is read-only, idempotent or requires a fresh proposal, preventing the client from automatically repeating an uncertain non-idempotent mutation request.

capabilities.title: Detect duplicate command submissions
capabilities.outcome: A supported idempotency key maps repeated compatible submissions to the same command result, while reusing that key for different content yields an explicit conflict without another effect.

capabilities.title: Bound response payloads
capabilities.outcome: Large inspection results use declared pagination or explicit truncation metadata, and the server never silently returns a partial result labeled as a complete source or document export.

capabilities.title: Normalize transport error output
capabilities.outcome: Unexpected internal transport failures return a stable sanitized response without stack traces, absolute host paths, session tokens, credentials or fragments of a refused request body.

capabilities.title: Handle unavailable LAN connections
capabilities.outcome: Losing the LAN connection leaves visible drafts and current inspection context intact, and reconnecting requires a fresh status read before mutation controls become available again.

capabilities.title: Separate dashboard and API caching
capabilities.outcome: Responses declare appropriate caching behavior so session-bearing dashboard HTML and revision-sensitive API results cannot be reused as authority after a session or source target changes.

capabilities.title: Validate endpoint query duplication
capabilities.outcome: Repeated singleton query parameters are rejected or handled by an explicitly documented rule, preventing disagreement between the transport, validator and domain handler about the selected target.

capabilities.title: Report rate and concurrency limits
capabilities.outcome: Local request throttling reports its active scope and retry guidance while preserving in-flight confirmed commands and keeping basic health inspection available within documented resource limits.

capabilities.title: Inspect transport diagnostics locally
capabilities.outcome: A bounded transport diagnostics view lists method, route category, duration and outcome for recent local requests without exposing bodies, authorization values or private source paths.

families.name: Command proposals and atomic planning
families.scope: Revision-bound command proposals, effects, preconditions and commit decisions.
families.refusal: Refuse stale targets, invalid capabilities, overlapping writes and missing explicit confirmations before effects.
families.recovery: Discard canceled proposals without state changes and retain a reviewable explanation of failed preconditions.
families.feedback: Show semantic effects, affected owners and the exact revision checked by each proposal.
families.evidence: Compare complete temporary document and source states before proposal, cancellation, refusal and confirmed execution.

capabilities.title: Create revision-bound command proposals
capabilities.outcome: A supported edit first produces a proposal containing its command identity, target revision and declared effects, with no domain or source mutation during proposal creation.

capabilities.title: Inspect semantic command effects
capabilities.outcome: A proposal lists meaningful added, removed, changed or reordered objects and affected source owners so an operator can review impact before authorizing any implementation-specific file change.

capabilities.title: Validate command target kinds
capabilities.outcome: A command expecting a page, node or component refuses a target of another kind before evaluating its effects or modifying any existing document object or source mapping.

capabilities.title: Check command capability prerequisites
capabilities.outcome: Proposal creation explains missing capabilities and ownership support for the selected operation, and unavailable prerequisites cannot be bypassed by submitting the command directly through another client.

capabilities.title: Bind confirmations to proposals
capabilities.outcome: A required confirmation identifies one proposal and revision so confirmation text entered for an older or different operation cannot authorize a newly generated effect set or target.

capabilities.title: Cancel a command proposal
capabilities.outcome: An operator can cancel an uncommitted proposal and retain the original document and source bytes, with the interface returning to its prior selection and draft context.

capabilities.title: Expire stale command proposals
capabilities.outcome: A proposal becomes unavailable when its bound document or source revision changes, and execution requires a newly reviewed proposal instead of silently rebasing onto current content.

capabilities.title: Detect overlapping write sets
capabilities.outcome: A multi-effect proposal identifies overlapping or conflicting source and document writes and refuses atomic execution rather than allowing handler order to decide which result wins.

capabilities.title: Validate complete command preconditions
capabilities.outcome: Every declared precondition is checked before effects begin, and a failure names the relevant target and condition without partially applying earlier valid effects from the same proposal.

capabilities.title: Preview multi-object command scope
capabilities.outcome: A batch proposal enumerates its bounded target set and unaffected scope, preventing a selection change or later query result from expanding the effects after operator review.

capabilities.title: Compute proposal fingerprints
capabilities.outcome: Equivalent normalized proposals produce a stable content fingerprint that changes whenever target, revision, precondition or effect content changes, independent of presentation labels and timestamps.

capabilities.title: Refuse unknown command implementations
capabilities.outcome: A valid-looking command envelope with an unimplemented operation kind receives an unavailable result and cannot fall through to a generic source or arbitrary shell execution handler.

capabilities.title: Plan source and document promotion
capabilities.outcome: A supported hybrid command prepares both normalized document and source outputs and validates their consistency before a confirmed promotion can make either accepted state visible.

capabilities.title: Show command validation findings
capabilities.outcome: Proposal review groups blocking and advisory findings with target references, and execution remains unavailable while any required precondition or schema validation finding is unresolved.

capabilities.title: Separate planning from execution authority
capabilities.outcome: A client allowed to inspect or propose an operation cannot execute it without the command's independent required authority, confirmation and current revision checks at the commit boundary.

capabilities.title: Bound command batch resources
capabilities.outcome: A proposal exceeding declared target, effect, source-byte or execution budgets is refused with exact exceeded limits before creating backups or applying a partial subset of its intended effects.

capabilities.title: Review dependency-affecting commands
capabilities.outcome: A proposal that changes references identifies dependent objects and required migrations, and unresolved dependencies block the operation instead of silently deleting or retargeting those references.

capabilities.title: Preserve proposal review drafts
capabilities.outcome: Editing a proposal's user-facing notes or closing its review panel preserves the underlying accepted state and cannot itself confirm, commit or change the proposal's effect fingerprint.

capabilities.title: Inspect command implementation versions
capabilities.outcome: Each proposal records the handler and contract versions used to compute its effects so replay or later review can distinguish a compatible implementation from a changed semantic operation.

capabilities.title: Export command review metadata
capabilities.outcome: An explicit review export contains a bounded semantic effect summary, target revisions and capability requirements, with source bodies included only through a separately disclosed operator choice.

families.name: Command journal and undo history
families.scope: Accepted local command records, inverse effects, undo/redo and deterministic replay.
families.refusal: Refuse incompatible, stale or corrupted history instead of replaying against a different accepted state.
families.recovery: Apply undo or redo atomically and preserve original journal records when a replay cannot be validated.
families.feedback: Distinguish pending, committed, undone, redone and refused operations with revision-linked evidence.
families.evidence: Replay literal command sequences and compare complete document/source hashes across undo, redo and failures.

capabilities.title: Append accepted command records
capabilities.outcome: A successful supported command appends one immutable journal record identifying its input revision, resulting revision and bounded declared effects only after the atomic commit is complete.

capabilities.title: Inspect journal entries by target
capabilities.outcome: Operators can filter accepted command metadata by qualified target and command kind without exposing unrelated source bodies or changing the order and content of the underlying journal.

capabilities.title: Capture inverse command effects
capabilities.outcome: Supported reversible commands record an inverse effect description against the committed result, allowing review of what undo would restore without relying on current UI selection or labels.

capabilities.title: Preview one-step undo
capabilities.outcome: An undo proposal shows the exact command and affected scope to reverse, checks the current accepted revision and performs no change until the operator confirms that proposal.

capabilities.title: Apply one-step undo atomically
capabilities.outcome: Confirming a valid undo restores all declared document and source effects together, while any failed inverse precondition leaves the complete current state and journal unchanged.

capabilities.title: Preview one-step redo
capabilities.outcome: A redo proposal describes the original command effects and verifies that the current state matches the expected undone revision before offering a separately confirmed replay operation.

capabilities.title: Apply one-step redo atomically
capabilities.outcome: Confirming a valid redo reapplies the exact supported effect set and records its relationship to the original command without duplicating unrelated objects or rewriting earlier immutable journal entries.

capabilities.title: Reject stale history actions
capabilities.outcome: Undo or redo against a state changed outside the compatible journal sequence returns a conflict and preserves current data, original history and any retained operator review draft.

capabilities.title: Group related journal operations
capabilities.outcome: A reviewed command group exposes its bounded members and combined inverse scope so an operator can undo one intentional action without treating unrelated intervening commands as group members.

capabilities.title: Inspect history branches
capabilities.outcome: After undo followed by a new command, the journal shows the diverging history explicitly and does not present the displaced redo chain as automatically applicable to the new accepted state.

capabilities.title: Replay journal sequences in isolation
capabilities.outcome: A selected compatible command sequence can be replayed in a temporary document copy, producing a result revision and findings without mutating the active workspace or real source files.

capabilities.title: Verify journal revision chains
capabilities.outcome: Journal validation checks that each committed entry's input and result revisions form a coherent chain and refuses corrupted, missing or reordered links before exposing history actions.

capabilities.title: Detect unsupported inverse operations
capabilities.outcome: A command without a reviewed inverse is clearly labeled non-reversible, and the UI cannot fabricate an undo action by restoring only part of the command's declared effects.

capabilities.title: Retain immutable operation receipts
capabilities.outcome: History views preserve original command receipts and their timestamps while showing later undo, redo or failure records as separate related events rather than editing the accepted past.

capabilities.title: Bound journal replay resources
capabilities.outcome: Replay enforces explicit entry, source-byte and time budgets and reports an incomplete attempt without accepting a partial replay as the current document or a verified complete history.

capabilities.title: Export a scoped journal segment
capabilities.outcome: An explicit export includes a selected bounded journal segment and its required baseline identity, while warning when excluded dependencies make that segment insufficient for independent complete replay.

capabilities.title: Import journal data without execution
capabilities.outcome: Opening an exported journal validates and displays its metadata in an isolated review without automatically replaying commands, changing source files or granting their recorded authority to the current session.

capabilities.title: Compare replay with accepted state
capabilities.outcome: A replay verification compares its resulting canonical document and declared source outputs with the accepted result, reporting each mismatch without silently repairing either comparison input or active state.

capabilities.title: Explain undo storage boundaries
capabilities.outcome: History help identifies whether an operation can restore document state, source files or only metadata and makes clear which runtime, external or provider effects are outside its supported inverse scope.

capabilities.title: Recover after journal append failure
capabilities.outcome: If durable journal promotion fails, the operation returns an explicit incomplete or rolled-back result according to its contract and cannot advertise an unrecorded successful command as fully accepted history.

families.name: Document snapshots and recovery
families.scope: Local snapshots of accepted documents, reviewed source scope and restoration proposals.
families.refusal: Refuse invalid, oversized, incompatible or stale snapshot restores before changing current accepted state.
families.recovery: Keep a verified pre-restore checkpoint and restore only the explicitly confirmed eligible scope.
families.feedback: Display snapshot provenance, exclusions, revision differences and restoration availability honestly.
families.evidence: Restore isolated fixtures with failed promotion, changed targets, missing content and exact unaffected-scope comparisons.

capabilities.title: Create accepted document snapshots
capabilities.outcome: An operator can capture a snapshot of the current accepted canonical document with its revision, schema and declared source scope, excluding transient DOM handles and session credentials.

capabilities.title: Inspect snapshot provenance
capabilities.outcome: A snapshot view reports its source revision, capture time, schema version and supported restoration scope without treating a recorded build or provider receipt as current live verification.

capabilities.title: Name local snapshots
capabilities.outcome: Operators can label an existing snapshot without changing its immutable captured document, source digests, identity or creation provenance, and invalid labels leave the original snapshot metadata intact.

capabilities.title: Compare snapshot and current document
capabilities.outcome: A restore preview reports added, removed, changed and reordered objects between the selected snapshot and current accepted document while retaining both complete original comparison inputs unchanged.

capabilities.title: Select snapshot restore scope
capabilities.outcome: A restore proposal identifies the eligible pages or resources selected for restoration and explicitly preserves unselected state, dependencies and histories according to its documented scope rules.

capabilities.title: Check restore dependency closure
capabilities.outcome: A scoped restore identifies required referenced objects and refuses unresolved or conflicting dependencies rather than partially restoring a graph with broken relationships or silently expanding the selected scope.

capabilities.title: Create pre-restore checkpoints
capabilities.outcome: Before a confirmed restore changes eligible state, the system captures the exact current supported scope as a recoverable checkpoint or refuses when that required checkpoint cannot be stored.

capabilities.title: Confirm snapshot restoration
capabilities.outcome: A restore confirmation binds one snapshot, selected scope and current revision so later source or selection changes invalidate the reviewed proposal before any restoration can occur.

capabilities.title: Restore supported snapshots atomically
capabilities.outcome: A compatible confirmed restore promotes the complete declared document and source scope together, preserving unaffected state and leaving an explicit receipt identifying the resulting accepted revision and checkpoint.

capabilities.title: Undo a snapshot restore
capabilities.outcome: A supported restore can be reversed through its bound pre-restore checkpoint after checking the latest revision, with a preview explaining exactly which restored resources would change again.

capabilities.title: Validate snapshot content hashes
capabilities.outcome: Snapshot validation verifies declared document and source content digests before restoration, and mismatched or missing bytes prevent accepting the artifact as a usable recovery point.

capabilities.title: Refuse incompatible snapshot schemas
capabilities.outcome: A snapshot using an unsupported document or source adapter version remains inspectable as metadata but cannot be restored until a reviewed compatible migration or adapter is selected explicitly.

capabilities.title: Export portable snapshot bundles
capabilities.outcome: An explicit snapshot export contains its declared portable document, source artifacts and manifest, excluding credentials and machine-specific runtime state while listing capabilities that cannot travel with the bundle.

capabilities.title: Import snapshots for review
capabilities.outcome: Imported snapshot bundles are validated in a temporary contained location and shown as untrusted recovery proposals without automatically applying their content or executing scripts contained in the archive.

capabilities.title: Bound snapshot retention
capabilities.outcome: Operators can inspect local snapshot storage totals and a proposed retention action before removing recoverable points, with pinned or referenced checkpoints protected according to the explicit local retention policy.

capabilities.title: Pin recovery checkpoints
capabilities.outcome: A pinned checkpoint remains protected from automatic local retention cleanup and visibly identifies the command or restore review that depends on its captured recovery scope and content revision.

capabilities.title: Handle missing snapshot artifacts
capabilities.outcome: If a referenced snapshot artifact is unavailable, the UI reports the missing scope and retains current accepted state, rather than restoring only the remaining files as a complete recovery.

capabilities.title: Simulate snapshot promotion failures
capabilities.outcome: A temporary recovery rehearsal can inject a failed promotion and demonstrate the documented rollback boundary without replacing the real workspace, source files or operator recovery checkpoints.

capabilities.title: Inspect recovery readiness by target
capabilities.outcome: Recovery status distinguishes a verified document restore, supported source restore and unverified provider recovery, using exact artifact and target evidence rather than a single global ready indicator.

capabilities.title: Record restore rehearsal evidence
capabilities.outcome: A completed rehearsal receipt names the snapshot, isolated source basis, selected scope and compared hashes, keeping that local test separate from a real restore or production recovery claim.

families.name: Current repository inventory
families.scope: Bounded inventory of tracked routes, source metadata, dependencies and template extensions.
families.refusal: Refuse private, linked and unsupported inventories while retaining exact source provenance and exclusions.
families.recovery: Keep the last accepted inventory available when a rescan fails or detects unresolved changes.
families.feedback: Report observed repository identity, inventory revision and incomplete or inferred findings explicitly.
families.evidence: Compare inventories from temporary repositories with renamed files, partial routes, dirty work and unsupported stacks.

capabilities.title: Inventory tracked entry points
capabilities.outcome: A repository inventory identifies declared application entry points with exact source paths and evidence, distinguishing explicit configuration from inferred conventions without executing the inspected application.

capabilities.title: Inventory route declarations
capabilities.outcome: Supported route discovery records route patterns and their declared source modules, while dynamic or ambiguous route generation remains a labeled unresolved finding rather than an invented route list.

capabilities.title: Inventory shared shell sources
capabilities.outcome: The current-repository inventory identifies declared shared header, footer and navigation sources so later edit proposals can explain which pages may share those authored modules.

capabilities.title: Inventory source component exports
capabilities.outcome: Supported static export discovery lists component candidates and their source revision without importing or executing repository modules merely to decide whether they are reusable components.

capabilities.title: Inspect dependency declarations
capabilities.outcome: An inventory reports declared direct dependency names and ranges from reviewed manifests without installing packages, reading registry credentials or claiming those declarations match current physical runtime versions.

capabilities.title: Inspect runtime pin declarations
capabilities.outcome: The inventory reports project runtime pins and engine declarations independently, identifying inconsistent declarations without changing the installed runtime or rewriting the project's intended platform baseline.

capabilities.title: Inspect build target declarations
capabilities.outcome: Supported build configuration discovery identifies declared output directories and public asset roots while marking computed or unsupported configuration as unresolved instead of executing it during inventory.

capabilities.title: Inspect Firebase configuration boundaries
capabilities.outcome: Inventory metadata distinguishes checked-in emulator or provider configuration declarations from an actual running emulator, authenticated provider account or deployed resource state for the selected repository.

capabilities.title: Inspect development bridge declarations
capabilities.outcome: The inventory identifies declared local builder bridge routes and their development-only guards, with unsupported proxy configurations reported rather than assumed to provide equivalent isolation behavior.

capabilities.title: Report inventory source revisions
capabilities.outcome: Every accepted inventory records the exact inspected source revisions and relevant file digests, allowing a later comparison to distinguish changed repository inputs from presentation-only list ordering.

capabilities.title: Compare repository inventory scans
capabilities.outcome: A rescan comparison lists added, removed and changed eligible resources with their original identities, preserving the previous inventory until the new result passes its validation rules.

capabilities.title: Handle dirty repository inventory
capabilities.outcome: Inventory reports staged, unstaged and untracked source state separately from commit identity, and never treats equal branch pointers as proof that the inspected working files are clean.

capabilities.title: Expose unsupported stack findings
capabilities.outcome: An unsupported framework or configuration produces a bounded capabilities report naming available read-only inventory and missing adapters without modifying the repository to force a recognized stack shape.

capabilities.title: Bound inventory filesystem work
capabilities.outcome: Scans enforce declared directory, file, byte and elapsed-work budgets and report exclusions, preventing vendor trees, runtime state or recursive links from expanding a normal repository inventory unexpectedly.

capabilities.title: Inspect workspace resource ownership
capabilities.outcome: Each inventoried resource identifies its repository, host extension or managed release ownership boundary so downstream imports and visual edits cannot accidentally modify an immutable upstream snapshot.

capabilities.title: Inventory public asset metadata
capabilities.outcome: Eligible public assets receive bounded path, media type and size metadata without recursively opening arbitrary file bodies or claiming that source presence proves successful browser rendering.

capabilities.title: Inspect source metadata conflicts
capabilities.outcome: Conflicting route, component or page declarations produce explicit findings with source references, and the inventory does not resolve the conflict by silently choosing whichever file was encountered first.

capabilities.title: Export repository inventory metadata
capabilities.outcome: An explicit inventory export contains only its declared eligible resource metadata, source revisions and exclusions, leaving private files, source bodies, credentials and runtime records outside the portable result.

capabilities.title: Revalidate inventory before proposals
capabilities.outcome: A proposal depending on inventory facts checks the relevant source revisions again, and changed declarations require a rescan or reconciliation instead of authorizing effects from stale repository metadata.

capabilities.title: Retain inventory interpretation provenance
capabilities.outcome: Inventory findings identify the adapter and rule version that interpreted each supported declaration, keeping an inferred framework convention distinct from a literal source fact during later review.

families.name: External project inspection and adoption
families.scope: Explicitly selected external project inventories and reviewed adapter adoption proposals.
families.refusal: Inventory is read-only by default; refuse automatic bridge installation, secret reads or source rewriting.
families.recovery: Cancel adoption without effects and preserve original project records through failed proposed migrations.
families.feedback: Show selected project boundary, unsupported source and every proposed file effect before acceptance.
families.evidence: Inspect temporary external projects with private files, unsupported frameworks and interrupted adoption rehearsals.

capabilities.title: Choose an external inspection root
capabilities.outcome: An operator explicitly selects one local project root for inventory, and the inspector confirms that boundary before reading eligible public project metadata within the chosen directory.

capabilities.title: Preview external scan eligibility
capabilities.outcome: A scan preview lists eligible resource categories, excluded private paths and active budgets without installing a bridge, running project scripts or opening arbitrary source bodies in advance.

capabilities.title: Detect external repository identity
capabilities.outcome: Inspection reports the selected project's observed repository identity and working state while avoiding assumptions that its origin, branch or owner authorizes writes from the current LAN session.

capabilities.title: Inspect unsupported external projects
capabilities.outcome: An external project with no supported adapter still receives a bounded read-only findings report, with unavailable operations clearly distinguished from absent files or a failed runtime launch.

capabilities.title: Map external resources for review
capabilities.outcome: A proposed mapping shows which external pages, components and assets could be represented by supported adapters without copying source into the active template or changing the external project.

capabilities.title: Explain external secret exclusions
capabilities.outcome: The inspection report identifies excluded secret and runtime categories without listing their contents, and requested path manipulation cannot expand inventory into those excluded locations or linked ancestors.

capabilities.title: Review adapter adoption requirements
capabilities.outcome: Before enabling an adapter, the operator sees its required source annotations, generated files, runtime bridge and unsupported round-trip cases for the explicitly selected external project boundary.

capabilities.title: Preview bridge installation effects
capabilities.outcome: A bridge proposal lists exact eligible configuration and source changes with revisions, backups and rollback scope, performing no installation until the operator reviews and confirms that proposal.

capabilities.title: Keep external scans separate
capabilities.outcome: Results from multiple external project inspections remain separately qualified by project identity and source revision, preventing matching relative paths from becoming shared writable targets across projects.

capabilities.title: Import external metadata into isolation
capabilities.outcome: A reviewed import creates a contained staging representation of eligible external metadata and source references, while the original project and active accepted document remain unchanged until explicit adoption.

capabilities.title: Compare external adoption alternatives
capabilities.outcome: An operator can compare inventory-only, source-owned adapter and document-owned generation proposals, with each alternative declaring supported operations, files affected and ownership consequences before selection.

capabilities.title: Refuse incompatible adoption targets
capabilities.outcome: Adoption refuses unsupported runtime versions, conflicting ownership or unrecognized configuration preconditions instead of replacing project files with a familiar template merely to satisfy the adapter's assumptions.

capabilities.title: Preserve downstream project records
capabilities.outcome: A supported adoption proposal identifies existing project context, tasks and memory as preserved downstream records, and a verified import cannot replace them with template history or blank upstream seeds.

capabilities.title: Rehearse external adoption locally
capabilities.outcome: A proposed adoption can run against an owned temporary copy and produce effect and rollback evidence without treating that rehearsal as permission to change the real external project.

capabilities.title: Bind adoption to inspected revisions
capabilities.outcome: Executing a confirmed adoption rechecks the selected project's inspected revisions and refuses drift before promoting bridge or adapter changes into that project's current source files.

capabilities.title: Cancel external adoption proposals
capabilities.outcome: Canceling a staged adoption removes only its owned temporary proposal artifacts and leaves the external repository, current template, existing project records and active local sessions unchanged.

capabilities.title: Detect preexisting external bridges
capabilities.outcome: Inspection identifies a compatible or customized existing bridge and proposes a reviewed reconciliation path instead of blindly installing a second control layer or overwriting its configuration.

capabilities.title: Export external inspection findings
capabilities.outcome: An explicit findings export contains qualified public inventory metadata, unsupported cases and proposed requirements, excluding external source bodies and private project records unless separately disclosed and selected.

capabilities.title: Review external project detachment
capabilities.outcome: A detachment proposal explains which reviewed integration artifacts could be removed and which authored changes or project records must remain, without automatically resetting the project to an earlier snapshot.

capabilities.title: Record external adoption evidence
capabilities.outcome: An accepted local adoption receipt identifies inspected and resulting revisions, exact effect scope and rollback artifacts while keeping runtime launch, provider access and production acceptance as separate observations.

families.name: Advanced Navigator discovery
families.scope: Extended runtime hierarchy discovery, filtering and stable expansion beyond the accepted basic Navigator.
families.refusal: Respect same-origin boundaries and explicit scan budgets; do not claim discovery of unmounted or inaccessible content.
families.recovery: Preserve valid expansion context and explain unavailable targets after renderer or document replacement.
families.feedback: Expose hierarchy scope, omitted content, grouping rules and filter effects without harvesting private subtree text.
families.evidence: Exercise shadow roots, nested frames, virtualized lists, repeated labels and large dynamic DOM fixtures.

capabilities.title: Inspect supported open shadow roots
capabilities.outcome: The Navigator can include explicitly supported open shadow roots as labeled boundaries, preserving host context while refusing to imply access to closed or otherwise inaccessible shadow content.

capabilities.title: Inspect same-origin nested frames
capabilities.outcome: An operator can enter an eligible same-origin nested preview frame with its own qualified hierarchy scope, and returning restores the parent context without reusing stale child-frame handles.

capabilities.title: Label inaccessible frame boundaries
capabilities.outcome: Cross-origin or unavailable nested frames appear as explicit non-expandable boundaries, with their excluded inspection scope disclosed instead of triggering hidden cross-origin access attempts or fabricating child elements.

capabilities.title: Filter hierarchy by semantic element kind
capabilities.outcome: Operators can restrict visible hierarchy results to selected semantic element kinds while preserving ancestor context and accurately reporting how many inspected elements matched the active kind filter.

capabilities.title: Filter hierarchy by visibility state
capabilities.outcome: A visibility filter distinguishes rendered, hidden, inert and unavailable-box nodes using disclosed criteria, without changing element attributes, app focus or visibility merely to include them in results.

capabilities.title: Filter hierarchy by source mapping state
capabilities.outcome: Operators can find mapped, unmapped, stale and read-only nodes in the inspected range, with results linked to ownership metadata rather than inferred from visible content or class names.

capabilities.title: Preserve expansion by durable identity
capabilities.outcome: When supported durable node mappings survive a preview rerender, the Navigator restores compatible expansion choices by identity while leaving ambiguous or replaced nodes collapsed and explicitly unresolved.

capabilities.title: Group declared component instances
capabilities.outcome: Supported component instances can appear under labeled definition groups without altering their actual DOM order, preserving qualified instance identity when an operator selects or reveals one grouped item.

capabilities.title: Inspect virtualized hierarchy coverage
capabilities.outcome: The Navigator identifies currently mounted inspectable items in a virtualized list and distinguishes them from total logical items, without describing an incomplete DOM scan as complete source coverage.

capabilities.title: Compare runtime hierarchy snapshots
capabilities.outcome: A read-only comparison highlights added, removed and reparented inspected nodes between two bounded snapshots, keeping transient DOM changes separate from accepted source or canonical document edits.

capabilities.title: Search hierarchy with scoped predicates
capabilities.outcome: A reviewed search syntax supports bounded combinations of tag, identifier, class and authored metadata predicates, with malformed or unsupported expressions refused rather than executed as arbitrary selectors.

capabilities.title: Show duplicate hierarchy labels
capabilities.outcome: Matching nodes with identical labels display bounded ancestor or source context that lets an operator distinguish targets without exposing aggregated child text or renaming the underlying application elements.

capabilities.title: Bookmark qualified hierarchy targets
capabilities.outcome: Operators can save a nonsecret bookmark for a durable supported target and resolve it explicitly, with missing or ambiguous matches reported instead of selecting another row at its former position.

capabilities.title: Reveal ancestor chains progressively
capabilities.outcome: For a deeply nested supported target, Reveal exposes the relevant ancestor chain in bounded steps and reports depth or row limits without implying that omitted ancestors were inspected completely.

capabilities.title: Filter hierarchy to a selected subtree
capabilities.outcome: An operator can focus inspection on a selected current subtree, with a visible scope marker and explicit return action that restores the broader inspected hierarchy without changing the application DOM.

capabilities.title: Inspect hierarchy mutation activity
capabilities.outcome: A bounded activity view summarizes structural mutation categories and affected qualified nodes without recording private text, input values or every unbounded event from a rapidly updating preview.

capabilities.title: Pause hierarchy observation explicitly
capabilities.outcome: Operators can pause live hierarchy refresh, see that the snapshot is frozen, and resume with a newly validated current-document scan rather than selecting stale paused targets as current elements.

capabilities.title: Explain hierarchy truncation locations
capabilities.outcome: When a scan reaches a node or depth budget, the Navigator marks the omitted branch boundary and distinguishes unknown descendants from inspected branches that genuinely contain no matching elements.

capabilities.title: Synchronize hierarchy hover by identity
capabilities.outcome: Hovering a supported hierarchy row highlights only its qualified current preview element, and clearing or replacing that element removes the highlight without applying source styles or changing selection.

capabilities.title: Navigate hierarchy inspection history
capabilities.outcome: Operators can return through recent qualified Navigator scopes and selections, with each history target revalidated against the current preview document before focus or reveal is attempted.

families.name: Selection and cross-surface context
families.scope: Qualified selection sets, hit-testing rules and synchronization between canvas, tree and source surfaces.
families.refusal: Refuse stale, foreign-document and incompatible multi-selection targets before editing or focus transfer.
families.recovery: Retain valid selection members and disclose removed targets after rerender or reconciliation.
families.feedback: Show selected scope, count, ownership and unavailable operations consistently across panels.
families.evidence: Use nested and overlapping fixtures, keyboard flows, rerenders and cross-surface source comparisons.

capabilities.title: Select multiple compatible objects
capabilities.outcome: Operators can create a bounded multi-selection of supported objects, with stable qualified identities and an explicit selection count that does not imply every member supports the same edit operations.

capabilities.title: Toggle selection membership by keyboard
capabilities.outcome: Keyboard modifiers can add or remove one eligible focused object from a selection set while preserving focus, existing members and the documented distinction between navigation and editing actions.

capabilities.title: Select a contiguous hierarchy range
capabilities.outcome: A range selection includes the eligible visible hierarchy rows between an explicit anchor and endpoint, reporting excluded incompatible boundaries without silently selecting collapsed or uninspected descendants.

capabilities.title: Preview box selection scope
capabilities.outcome: A canvas selection rectangle previews eligible current elements and exclusions before accepting a bounded selection set, without changing layout, source content or underlying application interaction behavior.

capabilities.title: Choose overlapping canvas targets
capabilities.outcome: An operator can inspect a bounded list of eligible elements under a canvas point and explicitly choose one, with ancestor and ownership context distinguishing overlapping targets with similar labels.

capabilities.title: Respect declared selection locks
capabilities.outcome: A locked object remains inspectable through an explicit alternate action but is excluded from normal hit selection, with visible lock state that never implies source permissions.

capabilities.title: Select through transparent overlays explicitly
capabilities.outcome: A deliberate selection action can cycle through eligible overlay layers in the current preview, showing each candidate and preserving the application's own event behavior while Interact mode is active.

capabilities.title: Inspect multi-selection capability intersections
capabilities.outcome: The inspector shows only operations supported by every selected object or explicitly identifies per-member exclusions, preventing one unsupported owner or target kind from being silently omitted during a batch edit.

capabilities.title: Preserve selection through compatible rerenders
capabilities.outcome: A supported durable selection can reconcile across a compatible preview rerender, while replaced, unmapped or ambiguous members are reported and never redirected solely by their previous row index.

capabilities.title: Show removed selection members
capabilities.outcome: If selected objects disappear, the interface identifies which qualified members became unavailable and retains unaffected valid members instead of clearing or retargeting the entire selection without explanation.

capabilities.title: Synchronize canvas and source selection
capabilities.outcome: Choosing a supported source object selects its qualified preview representation when available and shows an unmapped result when no current rendered counterpart can be resolved safely.

capabilities.title: Inspect selection ownership summaries
