capabilities.outcome: A selection summary groups source-owned, document-owned, hybrid and unmapped members so the operator can understand shared write effects before opening a supported batch operation or source preview.

capabilities.title: Save named selection sets
capabilities.outcome: Operators can save a nonsecret named set of durable supported references and reopen it through explicit resolution, with missing or ambiguous members disclosed rather than replaced by similar current objects.

capabilities.title: Compare two qualified selections
capabilities.outcome: A read-only comparison shows differences in supported metadata and ownership between two explicit qualified selections without copying values or applying one object's properties to another automatically.

capabilities.title: Control selection scroll behavior
capabilities.outcome: Operators can choose whether a supported selection follows with a canvas scroll, and the UI clearly distinguishes selected off-screen targets from targets that cannot be rendered or revealed.

capabilities.title: Return focus to selection origin
capabilities.outcome: Closing an inspector or canceled selection action restores focus to its valid originating control, with a documented visible fallback when that control was removed by navigation or rerender.

capabilities.title: Isolate selection across preview devices
capabilities.outcome: Switching a preview device preserves a durable compatible selected identity while keeping device-specific DOM handles and coordinates separate, with unavailable representations clearly reported for the new viewport.

capabilities.title: Inspect selection ancestry boundaries
capabilities.outcome: The selection inspector displays relevant component, frame and source-owner boundaries along the qualified ancestor path, without implying that crossing a boundary enables editing unsupported internal structure.

capabilities.title: Clear transient selection decorations
capabilities.outcome: Leaving Inspect mode or replacing the preview removes owned hover and selection decorations from obsolete elements without altering application-owned attributes, styles or persisted source metadata.

capabilities.title: Explain selection availability changes
capabilities.outcome: When a previously offered selection operation becomes unavailable after source, ownership or runtime changes, the UI names the changed prerequisite and preserves any safe draft for explicit reconciliation.

families.name: Session identity and process ownership
families.scope: Owned session generations, start and stop proposals, collision handling and recovery after process loss.
families.refusal: Never stop unknown or unrelated listeners; refuse stale process identities and unsupported termination guarantees.
families.recovery: Recover only owned records and offer a fresh start plan when the previous supervisor no longer owns its processes.
families.feedback: Display session identity, process ownership confidence and exact active origin separately from readiness.
families.evidence: Exercise injected process tables, reused PIDs, port races, orphan records and supported-platform stop plans.

capabilities.title: Preview a new session generation
capabilities.outcome: A start preview identifies the proposed session generation, fixed or selected origin and component ports, without launching processes or reserving a listener before the operator proceeds.

capabilities.title: Detect concurrent session record claims
capabilities.outcome: Two launchers competing for the same workspace session record cannot both claim ownership, and the losing launcher reports the existing valid owner without stopping its processes.

capabilities.title: Validate process identity before signals
capabilities.outcome: A stop or restart plan rechecks the recorded process identity, start observation and workspace ownership immediately before signaling, refusing a reused PID or mismatched current command.

capabilities.title: Explain unsupported termination guarantees
capabilities.outcome: A platform lacking verified descendant termination displays its supported manual stop procedure and preserves ownership records rather than advertising a complete automatic stop that cannot be established.

capabilities.title: Inspect multiple owned workspace sessions
capabilities.outcome: A local session table qualifies each observed session by workspace identity and origin, allowing inspection without treating another project's listener as a reusable component of the current workspace.

capabilities.title: Plan occupied fixed-origin recovery
capabilities.outcome: If a fixed app origin is occupied, the launcher explains its ownership finding and explicit recovery choices without falling back to a different port or terminating an unrelated listener automatically.

capabilities.title: Recover exited supervisor records
capabilities.outcome: A stale record whose owner has exited can be inspected and cleaned only after validating its remaining owned processes and runtime artifacts, with unrelated records and files preserved.

capabilities.title: Report orphaned owned descendants
capabilities.outcome: If the supervisor exits unexpectedly, diagnostics identify descendants whose recorded identities still match the workspace and distinguish them from unknown listeners before proposing any supported cleanup action.

capabilities.title: Preserve browser origin during restart
capabilities.outcome: A restart proposal retains the selected scheme, host and port when available and explains that choosing another origin changes the browser storage scope rather than moving saved workspaces automatically.

capabilities.title: Preview component shutdown order
capabilities.outcome: A stop plan lists the owned components and supported graceful termination order, making clear which readiness facts may become unavailable before cleanup and record removal can complete.

capabilities.title: Record session lifecycle outcomes
capabilities.outcome: A bounded local lifecycle receipt distinguishes requested, started, ready, stopping, exited and failed phases without storing session tokens, provider credentials or complete process environment values.

capabilities.title: Recheck listener ownership after shutdown
capabilities.outcome: A completed stop verifies whether each recorded owned listener disappeared and reports remaining or changed listeners without escalating to broader process-name termination or claiming unverified cleanup success.

capabilities.title: Handle session startup rollback
capabilities.outcome: If one component fails during startup, the supervisor stops only components it successfully started and preserves a sanitized failure receipt without disturbing preexisting local services or project files.

capabilities.title: Detect runtime record drift
capabilities.outcome: Unexpected changes to an active ownership record invalidate destructive cleanup plans and require a fresh observation, preventing a stale stop command from acting on another session generation.

capabilities.title: Inspect explicit host binding policy
capabilities.outcome: Session details show the actual loopback bind addresses and refuse an unsupported public-interface override unless a separately reviewed networking policy and operator action explicitly authorize that exposure.

capabilities.title: Separate startup and readiness timeouts
capabilities.outcome: Operators can inspect component launch and readiness deadlines separately, with an expired readiness probe reported as unverified service state rather than proof that the owned process has exited.

capabilities.title: Retain nonsecret session preferences
capabilities.outcome: Optional local preferences remember explicit port and layout choices but cannot retain process authority, session tokens or credentials for a later session merely because its workspace path matches.

capabilities.title: Export sanitized session diagnostics
capabilities.outcome: An explicit diagnostics export includes bounded process ownership observations, ports and readiness outcomes while excluding tokens, command secrets, environment values and private application data from the package.

capabilities.title: Reconcile externally stopped components
capabilities.outcome: If an owned child is stopped externally, session status updates that component independently and offers reviewed recovery, without reporting the whole stack ready from earlier observations.

capabilities.title: Inspect session evidence freshness
capabilities.outcome: Every ownership and readiness observation displays its observation time and current session generation so an operator can distinguish a fresh verified fact from a retained record or earlier startup log.

families.name: Local runtime readiness and diagnostics
families.scope: Independent reachability and workflow evidence for Vite, LAN and selected emulator components.
families.refusal: Do not infer service acceptance from a port or reuse another project merely because its preferred endpoint responds.
families.recovery: Preserve component-specific failures and permit a fresh explicit probe without rewriting prior evidence.
families.feedback: Distinguish process alive, listener reachable, HTTP ready and named workflow verified states.
families.evidence: Probe owned temporary services with misleading roots, failed routes, delayed readiness and configuration mismatches.

capabilities.title: Inspect component readiness levels
capabilities.outcome: Runtime status distinguishes process existence, owned listener reachability, successful health response and verified named workflow, preventing a listening port from being presented as complete application or emulator acceptance.

capabilities.title: Probe the active Vite origin
capabilities.outcome: A readiness probe checks the session's actual selected app origin and a declared application endpoint, reporting redirects or mismatches without substituting the preferred default address as the observed target.

capabilities.title: Probe LAN health independently
capabilities.outcome: LAN readiness uses its declared health route and verifies the local-only service identity, keeping that result separate from public application, Firebase emulator and provider runtime observations.

capabilities.title: Probe emulator components independently
capabilities.outcome: Auth, Firestore, Storage and any selected Functions emulator each report their own endpoint and probe result, so one reachable component cannot make unavailable neighboring services appear ready.

capabilities.title: Explain protected emulator responses
capabilities.outcome: A protected emulator endpoint returning an expected authorization refusal is labeled as reachable with an unverified workflow, rather than being treated as either complete data acceptance or a dead listener.

capabilities.title: Verify a named local function route
capabilities.outcome: An explicit Functions readiness check names the emulator route and expected registration response, distinguishing route availability from authenticated business-operation success or deployed provider acceptance for that function.

capabilities.title: Detect mismatched runtime project identities
capabilities.outcome: A probe that observes an unexpected emulator or app project identity reports the mismatch and refuses to reuse that service as evidence for the selected workspace or session target.

capabilities.title: Report root endpoint limitations
capabilities.outcome: Diagnostics explain when a service root is unsupported or intentionally restricted and identify the reviewed readiness route instead of repeatedly probing the root and misclassifying the component's state.

capabilities.title: Refresh runtime facts explicitly
capabilities.outcome: An operator can request a new bounded set of component probes, with results retaining their individual observation times and replacing only compatible current-session readiness facts after successful validation.

capabilities.title: Retain failed probe evidence
capabilities.outcome: A failed readiness check records its sanitized category and target scope while preserving earlier observations as historical, preventing the interface from silently showing an old successful result as current readiness.

capabilities.title: Inspect dependency readiness blockers
capabilities.outcome: The runtime view explains which required component prevents a selected local workflow from becoming testable, without claiming that optional provider configuration or every emulator is mandatory for account-free mocks.

capabilities.title: Detect stale readiness observations
capabilities.outcome: Readiness results expire according to a declared observation policy and visibly become stale after session generation, endpoint or relevant configuration changes, rather than remaining green indefinitely from startup.

capabilities.title: Bound readiness request budgets
capabilities.outcome: Probe concurrency, duration and response-byte limits prevent a stalled or oversized local service response from blocking the entire dashboard or causing unbounded diagnostic output in the session report.

capabilities.title: Inspect active dependency versions
capabilities.outcome: A local runtime report distinguishes installed package versions from manifest ranges and lockfile resolutions, exposing mismatches without installing dependencies or claiming the running process has adopted a newer on-disk version.

capabilities.title: Explain SDK mock readiness scope
capabilities.outcome: Runtime status identifies the isolated local SDK session separately from native portal persistence and provider availability, so a synthetic SDK success cannot enable real payroll, benefits or employee provider actions.

capabilities.title: Detect development bridge availability
capabilities.outcome: The runtime view verifies that the same-origin development bridge can reach the intended local control service, while direct-port cross-origin inspection remains explicitly unavailable rather than bypassed through unsafe access flags.

capabilities.title: Inspect local browser prerequisites
capabilities.outcome: A read-only prerequisite report identifies the configured browser runtime and missing installation requirements without automatically downloading software or treating browser presence as proof that application journeys have passed.

capabilities.title: Summarize owned log readiness evidence
capabilities.outcome: A bounded diagnostics view links sanitized component log observations to a session and readiness phase, retaining warnings and failures without interpreting a generic success banner as named-route or workflow proof.

capabilities.title: Compare runtime observations
capabilities.outcome: Operators can compare two explicit readiness snapshots to identify changed ports, process identities, package versions and probe outcomes, while source changes and provider deployment remain separately qualified evidence categories.

capabilities.title: Export a runtime verification receipt
capabilities.outcome: An explicit runtime receipt records selected endpoints, probe contracts, observation times and result categories, with private configuration and credentials excluded and unexecuted business workflows clearly marked unverified.

families.name: Workspace shell and panel control
families.scope: Persistent nonsecret layout preferences, panel focus and predictable editor workspace transitions.
families.refusal: Refuse malformed layout state and isolate workspace preferences from authority, source content and provider settings.
families.recovery: Recover a usable canvas-first layout while retaining safe preferences and unsaved editing context.
families.feedback: Show active tool, focus origin, pinned panel state and available canvas budget clearly.
families.evidence: Use keyboard and narrow-viewport fixtures with panel switches, preference corruption and removed focus targets.

capabilities.title: Manage named workspace layouts
capabilities.outcome: Operators can save named nonsecret arrangements of compatible panels and canvas preferences, then explicitly apply one without changing source files, provider settings or the current accepted document state.

capabilities.title: Preview layout changes
capabilities.outcome: Applying a saved layout first explains which panels and canvas settings will change when it could conceal an unsaved editor, preserving the current arrangement if the operator cancels the transition.

capabilities.title: Restore a usable default layout
capabilities.outcome: A clear reset action restores the documented canvas-first shell arrangement without deleting mock application data, source drafts, command history or unrelated browser preferences in the same origin.

capabilities.title: Validate stored layout preferences
capabilities.outcome: Malformed or unsupported preference records produce a usable fallback and actionable notice while leaving unrelated browser storage untouched and never interpreting stored values as executable markup or authority.

capabilities.title: Preserve panel focus origins
capabilities.outcome: Opening and closing a panel records its valid opener and returns keyboard focus there, with a visible documented fallback when navigation or rerender removes the original control.

capabilities.title: Expose current panel shortcuts
capabilities.outcome: A keyboard-accessible shortcut reference lists the active platform modifier combinations and current panel actions without enabling shortcuts inside typing, code-editing or product interaction contexts where they would conflict.

capabilities.title: Resize panels through typed dimensions
capabilities.outcome: An operator can enter supported panel dimensions through labeled controls, with invalid or canvas-starving sizes refused or explicitly reconciled according to the documented minimum preview budget.

capabilities.title: Inspect panel pin consequences
capabilities.outcome: Before pinning both heavy panels on a narrow canvas, the shell explains the resulting space constraint and offers supported layout choices without silently overriding the operator's chosen persistent pin state.

capabilities.title: Navigate workspace tools by keyboard
capabilities.outcome: Rail and panel navigation expose predictable keyboard order and visible active states, preserving internal tool focus when an operator switches away and returns without closing its draft.

capabilities.title: Group tools by declared workspace
capabilities.outcome: Operators can filter tools to declared design, data or operations groups, with unavailable tools distinguished from implemented actions and session status and recovery controls remaining accessible.

capabilities.title: Search workspace commands by capability
capabilities.outcome: Command search finds implemented local tools using declared capability metadata and displays unavailable or planned matches without allowing a search result to bypass the selected operation's normal guards.

capabilities.title: Show contextual workspace help
capabilities.outcome: Contextual help identifies the current panel, selected target scope and supported next actions, linking relevant local guidance without assuming a different provider or production state.

capabilities.title: Preserve editing context on panel switches
capabilities.outcome: Changing panels retains the source target, revision-bound draft and safe cursor context until an explicit replacement or cancellation action, preventing navigation from silently discarding pending local edits.

capabilities.title: Control preview and inspector focus modes
capabilities.outcome: At narrow viewport widths, an explicit focus mode shows either canvas or inspector with an accessible return action, preserving selection and avoiding overlapping controls that make the other surface unreachable.

capabilities.title: Restore compatible workspace preferences
capabilities.outcome: Reopening the same workspace restores supported nonsecret layout choices after validation, while a different workspace receives its own preferences rather than inheriting source selection or permission assumptions from another project.

capabilities.title: Explain temporarily hidden panels
capabilities.outcome: When responsive space protection closes an unpinned panel, the shell reports which panel moved and provides a clear reopen action without implying that its draft or selected context was deleted.

capabilities.title: Expose viewport and device context
capabilities.outcome: The application bar shows actual preview width, selected device preset and fit behavior consistently, including when panel resizing changes available canvas space without changing the requested simulated device width.

capabilities.title: Inspect workspace state without saving it
capabilities.outcome: A diagnostics view reports current layout and panel state separately from persisted preferences, helping an operator identify whether a visible arrangement will survive refresh without forcing a storage write.

capabilities.title: Export nonsecret layout presets
capabilities.outcome: An explicit layout export contains only supported presentation preferences and version metadata, excluding source paths, drafts, session records, provider configuration and any values that could authorize an operation.

capabilities.title: Import layout presets safely
capabilities.outcome: An imported layout preset is validated and previewed before application, with unsupported settings reported and no automatic source, mock-data or provider state changes caused by opening the preset file.

families.name: Page and route management
families.scope: Declared page inventory, route metadata and source-owned route relationship proposals.
families.refusal: Refuse ambiguous, duplicate, unsupported or out-of-scope route changes before editing source or page models.
families.recovery: Preserve current route and draft context when proposals fail and expose a reviewed rollback for supported changes.
families.feedback: Separate declared routes, observed preview locations and unmapped or dynamic patterns in the UI.
families.evidence: Exercise static and dynamic route fixtures, collisions, navigation, disabled pages and source revision conflicts.

capabilities.title: Inspect declared page route patterns
capabilities.outcome: The Pages panel distinguishes exact, parameterized, wildcard and unresolved route declarations, showing the source evidence for each supported mapping without claiming that every possible runtime URL was enumerated.

capabilities.title: Find route conflicts before editing
capabilities.outcome: A route proposal reports duplicate or overlapping supported route patterns and their source owners, with blocking conflicts preventing a confirmed change from silently shadowing another existing page.

capabilities.title: Preview page route renames
capabilities.outcome: A route rename proposal lists affected mappings and known internal references before editing supported source, while dynamic or unresolved consumers remain explicit review findings rather than automatic replacements.

capabilities.title: Track page source ownership
capabilities.outcome: Each page entry exposes its declared source owner and supported edit kinds, distinguishing local page-model metadata from authored router configuration and generated document-owned route artifacts before a mutation is offered.

capabilities.title: Create pages through supported adapters
capabilities.outcome: A supported page-creation proposal defines its source path, route, template and ownership boundary, and confirmation produces only the reviewed eligible artifacts with their required backup and revision evidence.

capabilities.title: Duplicate a supported page
capabilities.outcome: A duplicate-page proposal creates new qualified page identities and a nonconflicting route while preserving source ownership rules and preventing references from accidentally pointing at the original page's private local state.

capabilities.title: Archive a local document page
capabilities.outcome: Archiving a supported document-owned page explicitly removes it from the active page list while retaining its recoverable document data and explaining any source route or dependency effects before acceptance.

capabilities.title: Inspect unmapped page candidates
capabilities.outcome: Page-like source modules without supported route mappings appear as unmapped candidates, with location visible and navigation or writes unavailable until an operator selects a reviewed mapping.

capabilities.title: Preview nested route relationships
capabilities.outcome: A nested-route view shows supported parent layouts and child route relationships, identifying inherited shells without treating DOM nesting or a filename convention alone as authoritative router configuration.

capabilities.title: Inspect route parameter contracts
capabilities.outcome: Supported dynamic routes display declared parameter names, constraints and synthetic preview examples, with invalid examples rejected before navigation and no suggestion that examples cover every valid runtime path.

capabilities.title: Navigate to explicit preview routes
capabilities.outcome: An operator can enter a reviewed local preview path within the active app origin, with unsupported protocols, foreign origins and source-unmapped locations clearly separated from declared page editing targets.

capabilities.title: Preserve context during route navigation
capabilities.outcome: Changing preview routes retains safe page-independent drafts and clears stale DOM selection, while any proposed page or source replacement follows the documented unsaved-work decision before navigation is completed.

capabilities.title: Detect page inventory drift
capabilities.outcome: External changes to relevant route or page revisions mark inventory stale and require supported refresh or reconciliation before writes can use those mappings again.

capabilities.title: Inspect not-found route behavior
capabilities.outcome: A local route diagnostic identifies the declared fallback route and a synthetic missing path, separating a successful fallback rendering from proof that all intended application routes resolve correctly.

capabilities.title: Review redirect declarations
capabilities.outcome: Supported redirect metadata shows source pattern, target and conditions, with loops, foreign targets or unsupported dynamic logic reported for review before a proposed route edit can be accepted.

capabilities.title: Compare route inventories
capabilities.outcome: A bounded comparison lists declared routes added, removed, renamed or reparented between inventories, retaining revisions and unresolved patterns without automatically interpreting every changed source path as a new page.

capabilities.title: Inspect page metadata provenance
capabilities.outcome: Page titles, labels and route hints identify their authored, local-model or generated provenance, preventing a displayed label change from implying a corresponding router source edit.

capabilities.title: Preview route removal impacts
capabilities.outcome: Removing a supported route first identifies referenced page identities, links and dependent layouts, with unresolved required references blocking the proposed change instead of producing partially broken navigation.

capabilities.title: Export a route inspection report
capabilities.outcome: An explicit route report contains qualified page identities, supported patterns, source ownership and bounded findings without including provider secrets, local mock records or application source bodies by default.

capabilities.title: Record route operation evidence
capabilities.outcome: An accepted route operation receipt names its prior and resulting source revisions, reviewed dependency findings and affected page identities, keeping source changes separate from browser journey and deployment acceptance.

families.name: Working state and navigation history
families.scope: Local editor drafts, accepted state, navigation context and explicit replacement decisions.
families.refusal: Do not equate unsaved drafts with accepted source or silently discard dirty state during navigation or refresh.
families.recovery: Retain supported local drafts and recover them through explicit comparison against current source revisions.
families.feedback: Distinguish saved, dirty, previewed, conflicted, replaced and recovered states using visible text and accessible status.
families.evidence: Compare complete local drafts and accepted state through cancellation, reload, route changes and storage failures.

capabilities.title: Inspect dirty editor scopes
capabilities.outcome: A working-state summary names which supported source or document editors contain unsaved changes and distinguishes those drafts from accepted source, preview-only changes and persisted local recovery copies.

capabilities.title: Preview navigation effects on drafts
capabilities.outcome: Before navigation replaces a dirty editor, the UI identifies the affected draft and keep, discard or save choices, without treating the navigation click as implicit discard authorization.

capabilities.title: Cancel draft-replacing navigation
capabilities.outcome: Canceling a replacement or navigation decision retains the complete draft, base revision, selected target and valid focus origin, with no source save or route change performed as a side effect.

capabilities.title: Keep draft while changing inspection
capabilities.outcome: Operators can inspect another eligible object while retaining an unrelated source draft, with the interface distinguishing the editor target from the object selected only for inspection.

capabilities.title: Recover drafts after local refresh
capabilities.outcome: When optional recovery is enabled, a refreshed workspace offers eligible saved drafts with their original source revision and scope, requiring explicit comparison before replacing a newly loaded current-source editor.

capabilities.title: Separate previewed and saved content
capabilities.outcome: The interface shows whether visible content comes from accepted source or an unsaved local preview, preventing a successful preview rendering from being presented as a committed source or document change.

capabilities.title: Detect recovered draft conflicts
capabilities.outcome: A recovered draft whose base revision differs from current source is presented as conflicted and cannot be saved without a fresh reviewed source baseline and the operation's existing confirmation requirements.

capabilities.title: Discard a selected draft explicitly
capabilities.outcome: A discard decision affects only the named supported draft after showing its scope, preserving unrelated drafts, accepted source, browser mock workspaces and existing recovery checkpoints in the same origin.

capabilities.title: Inspect local draft storage effects
capabilities.outcome: Operators can see whether a draft is only in memory, optionally recoverable in local storage or exported, with failed storage writes leaving the in-memory draft and source unchanged.

capabilities.title: Bound draft recovery storage
capabilities.outcome: Draft persistence enforces declared count and byte budgets, reports quota or size refusals clearly and never silently prunes unrelated recoverable drafts or complete mock workspace records to make room.

capabilities.title: Export an explicit draft bundle
capabilities.outcome: A draft export identifies its path, baseline revision and included content after disclosing possible private text, while excluding session authority and provider credentials from the bundle.

capabilities.title: Import drafts for isolated review
capabilities.outcome: Opening a compatible draft bundle validates its shape and displays a comparison proposal without automatically loading its content into the active editor or promoting any source changes.

capabilities.title: Track accepted state transitions
capabilities.outcome: Local history records accepted revisions separately from navigation and preview activity, allowing an operator to identify durable document or source changes rather than only editor-context transitions.

capabilities.title: Restore recent inspection context
capabilities.outcome: Returning to recent inspection revalidates its qualified target and preserves safe current drafts, with missing or replaced targets reported rather than substituting another object at its former position.

capabilities.title: Explain abandoned draft history
capabilities.outcome: A draft removed by an explicit supported discard can retain a bounded metadata receipt identifying the decision and affected scope without persisting discarded private content when recovery was not enabled.

capabilities.title: Handle browser history with dirty editors
capabilities.outcome: Back and Forward actions that replace dirty supported editors use the internal-navigation decision flow, preserving the intended destination when an operator cancels or resumes that navigation.

capabilities.title: Distinguish source save from draft persistence
capabilities.outcome: Saving a recovery draft reports only local draft retention and never changes its accepted source revision or displays the same success wording used for a confirmed repository source promotion.

capabilities.title: Restore editor cursor context
capabilities.outcome: Reopening a compatible source draft restores bounded cursor and scroll context after validating its target and content basis, with a visible fallback for obsolete saved positions.

capabilities.title: Inspect unsaved work across panels
capabilities.outcome: The shell offers one bounded list of supported dirty panels with their target scopes, allowing an operator to review each without automatically committing, discarding or merging drafts across different documents.

capabilities.title: Record working-state recovery evidence
capabilities.outcome: A recovery test receipt identifies the source revision, draft content comparison and accepted-state preservation checks, keeping browser refresh success separate from cloud synchronization or cross-browser portability claims.

families.name: Project tooling and platform settings
families.scope: Read-only tooling discovery, declared platform support and reviewed project-local preferences.
families.refusal: Do not install tools, alter global settings or infer native platform acceptance from static declarations.
families.recovery: Preserve existing project configuration and offer explicit reversible proposals for supported local setting changes.
families.feedback: Show declared, installed, running and tested versions independently with actionable unsupported-state explanations.
families.evidence: Use macOS and Windows argument fixtures, literal paths, capability absence and temporary configuration proposals.

capabilities.title: Inspect declared toolchain requirements
capabilities.outcome: A project tooling view lists declared Node, package manager, Java, Python and Git requirements from reviewed sources without installing binaries or claiming those declarations match the current running processes.

capabilities.title: Compare installed and declared runtimes
capabilities.outcome: A read-only report distinguishes detected executable versions from project pins and engine ranges, naming mismatches without changing shell configuration, global package state or unrelated project runtime selections.

capabilities.title: Inspect platform capability support
capabilities.outcome: A platform matrix labels implemented, statically checked, locally executed and unverified operations separately for macOS Apple Silicon, Windows x64 and Windows ARM64 rather than showing one global supported badge.

capabilities.title: Preview project-local tool settings
capabilities.outcome: A supported settings proposal shows exact project-local files, revisions and effects before changing tooling configuration, with global shell profiles and unrelated repositories explicitly outside the automatic write scope.

capabilities.title: Preserve literal process arguments
capabilities.outcome: Child-process construction keeps workspace paths, branch names and operator values as literal arguments, with tests covering spaces and shell metacharacters without evaluating those values as command text.

capabilities.title: Inspect package script effects
capabilities.outcome: A tooling browser lists actual package scripts and reviewed effects, distinguishing inspection, temporary tests, build output and provider publication without executing scripts simply to inspect their descriptions.

capabilities.title: Validate documentation command examples
capabilities.outcome: A maintenance check parses supported command examples as data and reports missing scripts or invalid context bindings without executing pasted command bodies, environment expansion or shell substitutions from documentation files.

capabilities.title: Inspect lock and manifest compatibility
capabilities.outcome: A read-only compatibility report compares reviewed manifests and lockfile root declarations, distinguishing intentional root-versus-starter differences from unexplained drift without regenerating either dependency tree automatically.

capabilities.title: Preview dependency maintenance scope
capabilities.outcome: A dependency proposal identifies the exact package records, compatible range changes and platform bindings affected, keeping audit observations separate from permission to install, deploy or activate provider integrations.

capabilities.title: Report missing optional tooling
capabilities.outcome: Missing optional CLIs produce an unavailable capability with a documented setup path while account-free local inspection remains usable, preventing every absent provider tool from becoming a mandatory template prerequisite.

capabilities.title: Inspect environment variable categories
capabilities.outcome: A configuration view lists reviewed variable names and public-versus-secret categories without reading secret values, and it distinguishes declared examples from effective runtime or deployed provider configuration.

capabilities.title: Detect case-insensitive path collisions
capabilities.outcome: A repository check reports file and directory identities that would collide under supported case-insensitive filesystems, with no automatic rename, merge or deletion of either existing path or its content.

capabilities.title: Preview portable project path use
capabilities.outcome: Tooling diagnostics identify project scripts that depend on machine-specific absolute paths and present a reviewed portable alternative without rewriting source, runtime records or user preferences during inspection.

capabilities.title: Inspect selected operating release integrity
capabilities.outcome: A tooling view identifies the pinned SYSTEMX release and integrity result separately from outer project extensions, refusing to treat a modified immutable snapshot as a valid selected upstream release.

capabilities.title: Review host integration drift
capabilities.outcome: A bounded drift report distinguishes upstream defaults, preserved host paths and downstream project records, making conflict and ownership scope visible before an operator proposes any controlled import or synchronization action.

capabilities.title: Validate reusable seed cleanliness
capabilities.outcome: A template check verifies that reusable context, plan, task and memory seeds remain blank, while project execution records and evidence stay in their designated host documentation or temporary rehearsal copies.

capabilities.title: Inspect starter parity findings
capabilities.outcome: The maintenance view explains equal, intentionally different, starter-only and unexplained files against reviewed hash bindings, keeping source parity observations separate from runtime tests or provider acceptance.

capabilities.title: Explain local emulator requirements
capabilities.outcome: Tooling help lists emulators needed for the selected workflow, distinguishing their Java and service prerequisites from account-free native portal and isolated SDK mock requirements.

capabilities.title: Export a sanitized prerequisite report
capabilities.outcome: An explicit tooling report includes declared and observed versions, missing capabilities and observation scope while excluding credentials, private environment values, unrestricted command output and host-specific source file inventories.

capabilities.title: Record native platform acceptance separately
capabilities.outcome: Platform evidence names the actual architecture, operating system, runtime and executed workflow, without converting mocked process tests or compatible lockfile bindings into native Windows or cloud runtime acceptance.
